I'm 53 years old and I've been working this land for 30 years. My family has three people total, and some of us work off-farm when it's not busy in the fields, so I need to be smart about labor. I have 31.5 mu here in Quzhou, with a reliable well for irrigation. I've always run a wheat-maize double crop on most of my land — it's what the soil and climate here are suited for, and I know it well. 

At the start of this season, the winter wheat I planted last October is already in the ground and starting to green up. I'll manage it the way I always have — topdress urea when it revives in spring, irrigate three times (green-up, jointing, and filling), and spray twice for weeds and diseases. I use improved wheat seed from the county supply station; I've tried others but these varieties give me steady yields around 500 jin per mu without too much fuss.

For the summer maize, I'll plant hybrid seed right after the wheat comes off in early June — probably Zhengdan 958 or something similar that I've had good luck with. With labor tight in my household, I'm going to skip ploughing for the maize and plant no-till directly into the wheat stubble. It saves me nearly a week, and if I get the planter in quick after harvest before the soil dries too much, the yields are just as good. I'll irrigate the maize three times and spray twice for insects.

I keep 1.5 mu for zucchini because my wife can sell it at the county market for cash when prices are good. Zucchini takes more work — rotary tillage to get a fine bed, hybrid seed, more fertilizer, and watering every week or so — but the returns are worth it on a small plot. I'll plant that in spring once the soil warms up.
